adds.title: Solberg Government Legal Gender Change Law - approved 6 June 2016, effective 1 July 2016
adds.summary: Approved 6 June 2016 and effective 1 July 2016, Norway's legal-gender-change law gives persons resident in Norway who experience belonging to the other gender than registered in the National Population Register the right to change legal gender by application to the tax office with no surgery, hormone or diagnosis requirement, with self-application from age 16, joint application with holders of parental responsibility for ages 6-16, restriction of under-6 changes to congenital uncertain somatic sex development documented by health personnel, and provides that changed legal gender governs application of other laws except for establishment of parenthood.

adds.title: Oslo Police District - bias-motivated crimes statistics 2018
adds.summary: In Oslo in 2018, 238 incidents were recorded as hate crime, up 20% from 2017 and up 66% from 2015, with lesbian, gay, bisexual and trans persons comprising 20% of cases as the second-most targeted group after ethnicity at 57%.

adds.title: Norwegian Institute of Social Research - 2019 report on hate speech
adds.summary: In Norway in the year to March 2019, 23% of LGBT people versus 10% of the general population experienced hateful comments, 15% versus 4% experienced threats, mostly repeated, and 16% versus 3% experienced eliminationist statements such as 'you shouldn't have been born' or 'you don't have the right to live,' with the disparity widening further when comments targeting gender identity and gender expression are included, occurring mostly online on Facebook, Instagram and comment sections and disproportionately among young, politically/online-active people and people with two or more minority characteristics, with observing such comments toward one's group alone producing feeling unsafe, while Norwegian criminal code protection against discriminatory/hateful comments in public covered ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation and functional ability and treated online audiences of 20-30 people as public.

adds.title: Norwegian Directorate for Health - 2020 guideline for gender incongruence
adds.summary: Since 2020 in Norway gender incongruence is not a mental disorder but confers entitlement to municipal and specialist healthcare under least-invasive-first, informed-consent and multidisciplinary assessment principles without psychiatric/psychological assessment as a precondition for gender-affirming care, with adult care requiring persistent incongruence, clarified somatic-psychiatric contraindications, information on irreversible effects and side-effects, fertility preservation and individualized follow-up before hormone therapy initiated mainly in specialist care after GP referral with GP/local hospital follow-up and before breast surgery at regional centres and genital surgery at the national treatment service for binary and non-binary patients with speech therapy reimbursed via Helfo on physician prescription and hair removal covered by health trusts, and with under-18 care centred on municipal supportive counselling and family care with no drug treatment for prepubertal children while puberty-delaying GnRH analogues after puberty onset and estrogen/androgen hormones may be provided only through the national treatment service after paediatric multidisciplinary assessment of maturity, development, psychosocial situation and coexisting conditions.
